ratings.comment: This professor is extremely dry and boring. The material does make you think about language and communication at a deeper level though, and is thought provoking. Exams and quizzes were very fair, and if you do the practice problems assigned and understand the main ideas, then you will do fine. Not too heavy of a workload.
"If you're not nice to a waiter, you're not a nice person."  Apparently Malcolm Forster was not taught this.  He needs to learn to respect people.

He is very hard to understand and is extremely boring. Most of the material I learned in high or I can teach myself using the textbook. I only go to lecture because attendance is mandatory. TA Josh is helpful, but comes off as not that approachable.
Overall a fairly easy course if you have had some college math or intro/HS logic.  Show up for class do the homework no sweat.  10 quizes 1 final and two quizes get dropped.
He's the worst lecturer on campus. Not clear at all. Contradicts himself.
Some of the concepts in this class are kind of difficult to grasp and lecture is very boring. But TA Matt is very helpful. I would recomend this class to anyone that wants to avoid math.

I loved this class, no thanks to Forster. TA Matt was fantastic and discussion cleared up all that we didn't learn in lecture. Forster is a nice guy with a cool accent, but he is not engaging AT ALL and sometimes completely incoherent. Despite this, I would still recommend the class to anyone who enjoys thinking critically and wants to avoid math.
Very clear lecturer.  Weekly quizzes are easy if you follow the lecture and understand his examples.  Very easy if you already think critically, but he will help you if you don't.

Lecture can be somewhat dry but examples in class are helpful to concepts. His cool New Zealander accent helps a bit. Second half of semester much more difficult than the first so important to attend class and do weekly homework.  Good class to fulfill the QUANT A requirement if looking to skip math department!

Many have put Prof. Forster down as boring but I found him to be engaging and he really likes to teach. Reason in Communication was a tough class because you have to unlearn many prejudices about language. TA John was excellent. Forster has a good wit, and he's a member of the National Science Foundation.

He has a cool accent but the class is really boring.  There are quizzes every week that arent too hard and you get to drop the 3 lowest quiz scores.  The final exam is cumulative. His lectures are right from the book so its okay to miss a lecture once in a while, but unless you are really interested in this stuff i wouldnt recommend this class.

While this is a boring class due to the subject matter, prof. Forster makes it very easy to understand.  Gives a ton of examples and stops frequently to welcome questions.  Lecture material is very similar to the text, so there really is no reason to read if you go to class.  Also, 70% of your grade is determined by weekly quizzes.  No midterms.

Class is confusing and boring.  He takes attendance.  If you are debating between this class and another class then don't take this one.  Believe me, you will be happy you didn't.   There were a couple kids in the class who did really well and they were engineering majors, this is not a good class for people who are genuinely interested in philo
He is a very generous grader.  Very helpful in office hours.  Sweet accent.  Class is easy
he was very difficult to understand during class but the readings explained everything perfectly, the tests weren't difficult and the grades were overly generous.  This was Ph. of Science

Forster was the worst prof I've had at UW. Unclear, talked to the board in a terrible accent, completely boring his examples were useless; T.A., Brad Majors was just as bad and even more unapproachable. If your going to take this class to prepare for the LSAT DON’T!
Awesome accent. Professor is nice when you get to know him. TA was pretty helpful. Lecture material was very similar to the book.

What is relatively easy material is confused by what are easily the most boring lectures I've ever suffered through. However, the TA (Thurow) for fall 2004, was excellent and clarified everything. fyi, most of lectures are spent watching prof's butt jiggle as he writes on chalkboard. not pleasant.
The Prof is confusing but if the TA is Novack then you are in good shape.

The course was good. The TA was what made the class. His examples were very confusing and did not present different information when one of the students said they did not understand. If you get a bad TA, then it will be hard. Novack is excellent.
I enjoyed the way the class was structured. He pretty much restates what's in the book, except his examples are usually more confusing. Amusing accent.
